L253.t: The Fourth Triunity — the Triunity of Energy Infinity
rows: The Father-Spirit
The Paradise Isle
The Unqualified Absolute
L253.d: The fourth triunity is the triunity of energy infinity. Within it the beginnings and endings of all energy reality, from space potency to monota, are eternalized. Its members are the Father-Spirit, the Paradise Isle, and the Unqualified Absolute. Paradise is the center of the force-energy activation of the cosmos and the cosmic focal point of the Unqualified Absolute. This triunity absolutely controls the fundamental units of cosmic energy and releases them from the grasp of the Unqualified Absolute in proportion to the appearance of subabsolute capacity in the experiential Deities. The grand universe and the master universe are only partial manifestations of the energy potential existing in this association. The revelator sums it up in a phrase: this triunity is force and energy.

L254.t: The Fifth Triunity — the Triunity of Reactive Infinity
rows: The Universal Father
The Universal Absolute
The Unqualified Absolute
L254.d: The fifth triunity is the triunity of reactive infinity. Its members are the Universal Father, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute; uniquely among the seven, the Father is its only Deity person and the other two are Absolutes of potentiality. This grouping eternalizes the functional infinity realization of all that is actualizable within the domains of nondeity reality. It manifests unlimited reactive capacity to the volitional, causative, tensional, and patternal actions and presences of the other triunities. Where the earlier triunities deal with will, pattern, spirit, and energy, this one deals with the capacity of the cosmos to respond to all of them. It shows that infinity could not function if there were action without response.

L255.t: The Sixth Triunity — the Triunity of Cosmic-Associated Deity
rows: The Universal Father
The Deity Absolute
The Universal Absolute
L255.d: The sixth triunity is the triunity of cosmic-associated Deity. Its members are the Universal Father, the Deity Absolute, and the Universal Absolute. The revelator defines it as the association of Deity-in-the-cosmos, the immanence of Deity in conjunction with the transcendence of Deity. God is beyond the cosmos and at the same time within it, and these two aspects are bound into one functional association. It is also the last outreach of divinity on the levels of infinity toward those realities which lie outside the domain of deified reality. The potential of Deity and the Absolute that unifies deified and undeified join the Father to form the farthest frontier that divinity reaches. Seeing transcendence and immanence as conjoined rather than opposed is a notable feature of this view of God.

L256.t: The Seventh Triunity — the Triunity of Infinite Unity
rows: The Universal Father
The Conjoint Actor
The Universal Absolute
L256.d: The seventh triunity is the triunity of infinite unity, the unity of infinity functionally manifest in time and eternity, the co-ordinate unification of actuals and potentials. Its members are the Universal Father, the Conjoint Actor, and the Universal Absolute. The Conjoint Actor integrates the functional aspects of all actualized reality from finites through transcendentals to absolutes, while the Universal Absolute perfectly compensates the differentials inherent in all incomplete reality. Here the Conjoint Actor and the Universal Absolute are alike responsive to Deity and nondeity presences, and the Father is conceptually indistinguishable from the I AM. The revelator adds that these seven are only part of the fifteen triune associations of the First Source and Center, eight of which are not revealed.

rows: The Eternal Son
The absolute of spirit reality, the absolute personality
The Paradise Isle
The absolute of cosmic reality, the absolute pattern
The Conjoint Actor
The absolute of mind reality; the existential Deity synthesis of personality and power
L257.d: Every triunity includes the First Source and Center, but there are triune associations of which the Father is not a member. The revelator calls these triodities and presents two, the first being the Triodity of Actuality. It consists in the interrelationship of the three absolute actuals: the Eternal Son, the Paradise Isle, and the Conjoint Actor. The Eternal Son is the absolute of spirit reality and the absolute personality; the Paradise Isle is the absolute of cosmic reality and the absolute pattern; the Conjoint Actor is the absolute of mind reality. Spirit, pattern, and mind are joined so as to co-ordinate the sum total of actualized reality, whether spiritual, cosmic, or mindal. Triodities are directly concerned with the cosmic appearance of the experiential Deities.

rows: The Deity Absolute
The Universal Absolute
The Unqualified Absolute
L258.d: The second triodity is the Triodity of Potentiality, the association of the three Absolutes of potentiality: the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute. Where the Triodity of Actuality co-ordinates actualized reality, this triodity interassociates the infinity reservoirs of all latent energy reality, whether spirit, mindal, or cosmic. It yields the integration of all latent energy reality and is infinite in potential. The revelator explains that triunities are primarily concerned with the functional unification of infinity, whereas triodities are directly involved in the cosmic appearance of the experiential Deities, the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Absolute. Because the reservoir of unrealized possibilities becomes the material of the growing Deities, this list exposes the deep foundation of an evolving universe.

L259.t: The Sevenfold Self-Relationship of the I AM
rows: The Universal Father
I AM father of the Eternal Son
The Universal Controller
I AM cause of eternal Paradise
The Universal Creator
I AM one with the Eternal Son
The Infinite Upholder
I AM self-associative
The Infinite Potential
I AM self-qualified
The Infinite Capacity
I AM static-reactive
The Universal One of Infinity
I AM as I AM
L259.d: The paper on Deity and reality portrays, as if in a time sequence, how the I AM by internal metamorphoses establishes the basis for a sevenfold self-relationship, so that finite minds may approach the idea of infinity. The concept of the solitary I AM and of the I AM as a triunity is now expanded to embrace the I AM as a sevenfold. Each phase is expressed in a brief declaration: father of the Eternal Son, cause of Paradise, one with the Son, self-associative, self-qualified, static-reactive, and finally I AM as I AM. The first three concern relationships of actualities, the next three the statics and potentials of reality, and the last the self-relationship of infinity itself. These seven phases then eternalize as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity.

rows: The First Source and Center
First Person of Deity and primal nondeity pattern, the Universal Father
The Second Source and Center
Second Person of Deity, the Eternal and Original Son
The Paradise Source and Center
Second nondeity pattern, the eternal Isle of Paradise
The Third Source and Center
Third Person of Deity, the Conjoint Actor, infinite integrator
The Deity Absolute
The totality of all Deity potential; the originator of destiny
The Unqualified Absolute
Static, reactive, and abeyant; totality of nondeified reality
The Universal Absolute
Unifier of the deified and the undeified
L260.d: The seven prime relationships within the I AM eternalize as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity. The revelator presents them in sequence, yet stresses that all seven are in reality unqualifiedly and co-ordinately eternal; picturing their beginnings is only a concession to the mortal mind. The list includes the three persons of Deity and the two nondeity patterns, the First Source and Center and Paradise, followed by the two Absolutes of potentiality and the Universal Absolute that unifies them. The content matches the earlier list of seven Absolutes, but here each Absolute is traced to a relationship within the I AM, so the order and the names differ. These seven constitute the beginnings of reality.

L261.t: Three Great Classes of Primordial Relationships
rows: Unity relationships
Relations within the I AM conceived as a threefold and sevenfold self-differentiation
Duality relationships
Relations between the I AM as sevenfold and the Seven Absolutes of Infinity
Triunity relationships
The functional associations of the Seven Absolutes of Infinity
L261.d: It has sometimes been said that unity begets duality, that duality begets triunity, and that triunity is the eternal ancestor of all things. Taking up this saying, the revelator sorts primordial relationships into three great classes. Unity relationships exist within the I AM as its unity is conceived as a threefold and then a sevenfold self-differentiation; duality relationships exist between the I AM as sevenfold and the Seven Absolutes of Infinity; triunity relationships are the functional associations of those Absolutes. The revelator condenses this into a single formula: the I AM is unqualified infinity as unity, the dualities eternalize reality foundations, and the triunities eventuate the realization of infinity as universal function. Pre-existentials become existential, and existentials become functional.

L262.t: Two Original Phases of Emerging Finite Reality
rows: Primary maximums
The supremely perfect reality, the Havona type of universe and creature
Secondary maximums
The supremely perfected reality, the superuniverse type of creature and creation
L262.d: The beginning of the finite marks the beginning of universe history and the coming into existence of time itself; to the creature mind there is no conceivable actuality prior to the finite. The revelator states that this newly appearing finite reality exists in two original phases. Primary maximums are the supremely perfect reality of the Havona type, perfect from the start; secondary maximums are the supremely perfected reality of the superuniverse type, perfected through evolution. They are the constitutively perfect and the evolutionally perfected, co-ordinate in eternity relationships but different within the limits of time, since what is growing must appear incomplete in time. The revelator adds that relationships between the two give rise to tertiary maximums, neither perfect nor perfected yet co-ordinate with both.

L263.t: Four Repercussions to the Creative Actualization of the Finite
rows: The deity response
The appearance of the three levels of experiential supremacy
The universe response
An activation of the architectural plans for the superuniverse space level
The creature repercussion
The appearance of perfect beings of Havona and perfected ascenders
The divinity response
The compensating presence of God the Sevenfold
L263.d: The promulgation of finite existences is a transference from potentials to actuals within the absolute associations of functional infinity. Of its many repercussions the revelator selects four. On the deity level, the three levels of experiential supremacy appear; on the universe level, the architectural plans for the superuniverses are activated; on the creature level, perfect beings of Havona and perfected evolutionary ascenders emerge. Yet attaining perfection by evolution implies a starting point short of perfection, and so imperfection arises within the evolutionary creation. The fourth repercussion is divinity's response to that very imperfection: the compensating presence of God the Sevenfold. Imperfection is no accident but the consequence of the time lag inherent in evolution, and God compensates for it.

L264.t: Ten Realities Associated with the Transcendental Level
rows: The Deity presence of the Ultimate
The concept of the master universe
The Architects of the Master Universe
The two orders of Paradise force organizers
Certain modifications in space potency
Certain values of spirit
Certain meanings of mind
Absonite qualities and realities
Omnipotence, omniscience, and omnipresence
Space
L264.d: Between the finite and the absolute lies the transcendental level, and the revelator names ten of the realities associated with it. Some concern personality and plan: the Deity presence of the Ultimate, the concept of the master universe, its Architects, and the two orders of Paradise force organizers. Others concern qualities of reality: modifications in space potency, values of spirit, and meanings of mind. Absonite qualities belong here too, as do the divine attributes of omnipotence, omniscience, and omnipresence. The list closes, strikingly, with space itself, which finite creatures take for granted as a mere background but which the revelator classifies as a transcendental reality. The universe exists on finite, transcendental, and absolute levels, the cosmic stage for the endless drama of personality performance and energy metamorphosis.

rows: Incomplete finites
The present status of ascending creatures and of Urantia mortals
Maximum finites
Experiential creatures who have attained destiny within the present universe age
Transcendentals
A superfinite level following finite progression; much of Paradise-Havona
Ultimates
That which is of master universe significance
Coabsolutes
The projection of experientials upon a supermaster universe field
Absolutes
The eternity presence of the seven existential Absolutes
Infinity
Pre-existential and postexperiential
L265.d: The paper on universe level associations begins by grouping the many forms and phases of reality in the grand and master universes into seven levels for conceptual convenience. At the bottom are incomplete finites, the present status of Urantia mortals; above them are maximum finites, creatures who have attained destiny within the present universe age. Then come transcendentals, ultimates, coabsolutes, and absolutes, and finally infinity, a hypothetical reality before all beginnings and after all destinies. The revelator notes that even the word maximum is relative: maximum of what, and in which universe age? These seven levels form the framework of the whole paper, locating where man now stands and where he is going on a cosmic map.

L266.t: Seven Limitations Conditioning the Concepts of Reality
rows: The limitations of mortal language
The limitations of the mortal mind
The limited development of the seven superuniverses
Ignorance of the six prime purposes of superuniverse development not pertaining to the mortal ascent
The inability to grasp even a partial eternity viewpoint
The impossibility of depicting cosmic evolution and destiny in relation to all universe ages
The inability of any creature to grasp pre-existentials or postexperientials
L266.d: Immediately after presenting the seven levels of reality, the revelator insists that they are only convenient compromise symbolizations for the present universe age and the mortal perspective. There are other ways of viewing reality, and the concepts presented are wholly relative. This list gives the seven conditions behind that relativity. It begins with the limitations of language and mind, then moves to the unfinished superuniverses, ignorance of the six prime purposes of superuniverse development unrelated to the mortal ascent, the lack of an eternity viewpoint, the impossibility of covering all universe ages, and finally the inability to grasp what lies before beginnings and after destinies. That the revelator sets out the limits of the explanation so systematically is significant: cosmology is offered not as a fixed map but as a provisional aid to growing understanding.

L267.t: Three Levels of the Trinity of Trinities
rows: The level of the three Trinities
The level of experiential Deity
The level of the I AM
L267.d: The Trinity of Trinities can be portrayed in several ways, and the revelator elects to present the three-level concept. The first is the level of the three Trinities, where the Paradise, Ultimate, and Absolute Trinities function as perfectly synchronized though distinct groupings. The second is the level of experiential Deity, the associative union of the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Absolute, who are genetically associated with these Trinities. The third is the level of the I AM. These are levels of increasing unification: the Trinity of Trinities is actually the first level, and the second and third are its unification-derivatives. The concept points to a possible unlimited integration of reality, embracing causes, intermediates, and finals, beginnings, existings, and destinies, and it stands among the summits of the cosmology of the Urantia Book.

L268.t: Three Human Factors in the Paradox of Experiential and Existential Viewpoints
rows: The limited human viewpoint
The inability to grasp the concept of unqualified eternity
The imperfect human status
The remoteness from the absolute level of experientials
The purpose of human existence
Designed to evolve by experience, hence dependent on experience
L268.d: The existential view that the Trinity of Trinities is already factualized and the experiential view that it is progressively actualized in time seem to clash. The revelator calls the paradox inevitable and traces the distortion of the time view to three factors on the human side. The first is the limited human viewpoint, unable to grasp unqualified eternity; the second is the imperfect human status, remote from the absolute level of experientials; the third is the purpose of human existence, for mankind is designed to evolve by the technique of experience and must therefore be constitutively dependent on it. Only an Absolute can be both existential and experiential. The list locates the paradox not in reality itself but in the position of the observer, and it invites the endless quest of discovery.

rows: Virgin Adjusters
Serving on their initial assignment in candidates for eternal survival
Advanced Adjusters
Having served one or more seasons with will creatures
Supreme Adjusters
Monitors whose human partners declined eternal survival
Vanished Adjusters
A fourth stage of service about which we are not sure
Liberated Adjusters
Eternally liberated from the service of time
Fused Adjusters—finaliters
One with the ascending creatures of the superuniverses
Personalized Adjusters
Served with incarnated Paradise Sons or achieved unusual distinction
L269.d: Adjusters are individuated as virgin entities, and all are destined to become liberated, fused, or Personalized Monitors. The revelator understands that there are seven orders of Adjusters but admits not fully comprehending the divisions. The orders follow the course of an Adjuster's career: the Virgin Adjuster on its first assignment, the experienced Advanced and Supreme Adjusters, the Vanished Adjusters whose trail is lost, and then the three final destinies of liberation, fusion, and personalization. The revelator openly notes that Melchizedeks and Solitary Messengers hold differing views about the fourth stage. The list shows that Adjusters, though eternally uniform in divine nature, become differentiated through the actual experience of universe ministry.

L270.t: Three Divine Injunctions to Beings of High Spiritual Orders
rows: Always to show adequate respect for the experience and endowments of their seniors and superiors
Always to be considerate of the limitations and inexperience of their juniors and subordinates
Never to attempt a landing on the shores of Divinington
L270.d: Divinington, home of the Adjusters, is the least known of the seven secret spheres of Paradise. Beings of high spiritual orders receive only three divine injunctions, and the third forbids any attempt to land on its shores. The first two read like the basic courtesy of universe society: upward, respect for the experience and endowments of seniors and superiors; downward, consideration for the limitations and inexperience of juniors and subordinates. This short list shows that the ethics of high beings rests not on elaborate codes but on the simple principles of respect and consideration. The narrator calmly reflects that it would be useless to go to Divinington anyway, and explains that knowledge of Adjusters must be gathered from a thousand and one different sources.

L271.t: Three Qualifications of the Human Candidate
rows: Intellectual capacity
Is the mind normal? Can the individual develop into a bona fide will creature?
Spiritual perception
The prospects of reverential development, the birth and growth of the religious nature
Combined intellectual and spiritual powers
The degree to which these two endowments may produce strength of human character
L271.d: Before assignment, a Thought Adjuster considers its human candidate, and the revelator describes three qualifications in which the volunteering Adjuster is particularly interested. The first is intellectual capacity: is the mind normal, and can the individual develop into a bona fide will creature in whom wisdom has an opportunity to function? The second is spiritual perception: the prospects of reverential development and of the birth and growth of the religious nature, the potential of soul. The third is the combination of the two, the degree to which intellect and spirit may be associated to produce strength of human character and contribute to the evolution of an immortal soul of survival value. Neither intellect nor spirituality alone is decisive; their co-operation is. On these facts, the revelator believes, the Monitors freely volunteer.

L272.t: Six Influences and Conditions Associated with Adjuster Arrival
rows: The assignment of personal seraphic guardians
The attainment of the third circle of intellectual achievement and spiritual attainment
Upon the making of a supreme decision of unusual spiritual import
The spirit of brotherhood
Declaration of intention to do the will of God
Influence of the Supreme Being
L272.d: On an evolutionary world before the pouring out of the Spirit of Truth, the bestowal of Adjusters appears to be determined by many spirit influences and personal attitudes. The revelator lists six observed conditions. Some follow universe administration: the assignment of personal seraphic guardians and the attainment of the third circle. Others depend on human attitude: a supreme decision made in a personal crisis, the spirit of brotherhood shown in love for one's fellows and unselfish ministry, and the quiet declaration of intention to do the will of the Father in heaven. Finally, on worlds where Adjusters do not fuse, they are sometimes bestowed in response to the influence of the Supreme Being. Brotherly love and the decision to do God's will open the door to the indweller.

rows: Has had requisite experience in the evolving life of a will creature
Has acquired the balance of spiritual power in a human who has made the third psychic circle
Has a subject who has made the supreme decision, a solemn betrothal with the Adjuster
Has a subject mustered into one of the reserve corps of destiny
Has been temporarily detached during human sleep to perform some exploit of liaison or contact
Has served in a time of crisis in a human who was the material complement of a spirit personality
L273.d: Adjusters are classified by experience as virgin, advanced, and supreme, but the revelator adds a functional classification: self-acting Adjusters. This list gives six conditions under which an Adjuster attains that status. They are requisite experience in a previous indwelling, the balance of spiritual power in a human who has made the third psychic circle, a subject's supreme decision and solemn betrothal with the Adjuster, a subject mustered into a reserve corps of destiny, some exploit of liaison performed while detached during human sleep, and service in a crisis within a human who was the material complement of a spirit personality. Notably, half of the conditions concern the Adjuster's own experience and half the achievements of the human subject. Such Adjusters possess a marked degree of will in matters not involving their immediate indwelling.

L274.t: Four Ways to Augment Harmony with the Adjuster
rows: Choosing to respond to divine leading
Basing life on truth, beauty, and goodness, co-ordinated through wisdom, worship, faith, and love
Loving God and desiring to be like him
Genuine recognition of the divine fatherhood and loving worship of the heavenly Parent
Loving man and sincerely desiring to serve him
Recognition of the brotherhood of man with wise affection for each fellow mortal
Joyful acceptance of cosmic citizenship
Honest recognition of progressive obligations to the Supreme Being
L274.d: The revelator cautions against regarding co-operation with the Adjuster as a particularly conscious process; yet motives, decisions, faithful determinations, and supreme desires do constitute real and effective co-operation. On that basis four ways are given to augment Adjuster harmony consciously. The first is choosing to respond to divine leading, building life on truth, beauty, and goodness. The second and third, loving God and loving man, correspond to the teaching of Jesus on the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man. The fourth is the joyful acceptance of cosmic citizenship, recognizing one's obligations to the Supreme Being and the interdependence of evolutionary man and evolving Deity. The revelator calls this the birth of cosmic morality and the dawning realization of universal duty.

L275.t: Three Ways the Conquest of Cosmic Evolution Is Reflected
rows: Adjuster attunement
The spiritizing mind nears the Adjuster presence proportional to circle attainment
Soul evolution
The emergence of the morontia soul indicates the extent and depth of circle mastery
Personality reality
The degree of selfhood reality is directly determined by circle conquest
L275.d: The seven levels of human progression, the psychic circles, are personal and vary with each individual's capacity for growth, so they are difficult to define precisely. Instead of defining them, the revelator shows three ways in which their conquest is reflected. First is Adjuster attunement: the spiritizing mind nears the Adjuster presence in proportion to circle attainment. Second is soul evolution: the emergence of the morontia soul indicates the extent and depth of circle mastery. Third is personality reality: persons become more real as they ascend from the seventh to the first circle. The last item is especially striking, for it means that spiritual growth is not acquiring more but becoming more truly real. So the child of material evolution grows into the mature human of immortal potentiality.

L276.t: Limits of the Psychic Circles — the Seventh, Third, and First
rows: The seventh circle
Entered when humans develop personal choice, moral responsibility, and spiritual individuality
The third circle
The Adjuster's work is much more effective after receiving a personal seraphic guardian
The first circle
The highest mind-Adjuster relationship; the Adjuster may speak directly
L276.d: The seven psychic circles of human growth cannot be precisely defined, but the revelator considers it permissible to suggest their minimum and maximum limits, and so describes only three of them. The seventh circle is the starting point, entered when human beings develop the powers of personal choice, individual decision, moral responsibility, and spiritual individuality. The third circle is a midpoint of transition, when a personal seraphic guardian of destiny is assigned and the Adjuster's work becomes much more effective. The first circle represents the highest mind-Adjuster relationship possible before the morontia soul is freed from the material body, when the Adjuster can ordinarily speak directly. The circles in between are left unnamed. The revelator suggests these circles might better be called cosmic levels.

L277.t: Three Factors in the Evolutionary Creation of an Immortal Soul
rows: The human mind
All cosmic influences antecedent thereto and impinging thereon
The divine spirit indwelling this human mind
All potentials inherent in such a fragment of absolute spirituality
The relationship between material mind and divine spirit
Neither material nor spiritual—morontial; it is soul
L277.d: The soul is often explained by two factors, mind and spirit, but the revelator states that there are three and not two factors in the evolutionary creation of an immortal soul. The first is the human mind with all the cosmic influences that bear upon it; the second is the divine spirit indwelling that mind, with all its inherent potentials. The third is the key: the relationship between material mind and divine spirit. This relationship carries a value and meaning found in neither contributing factor, and its reality is neither material nor spiritual but morontial; it is soul. The insight that a relationship itself gives rise to a new reality is the key to understanding the nature of the soul. The midway creatures have long called this evolving soul the mid-mind.

rows: Personality is bestowed by the Universal Father or by the Conjoint Actor
It may be bestowed upon any living energy system which includes mind or spirit
It is not wholly subject to the fetters of antecedent causation; it is relatively creative
In material creatures it causes spirit to strive for the mastery of energy-matter through mind
While devoid of identity, it can unify the identity of any living energy system
It discloses only qualitative response to the personality circuit
Personality is changeless in the presence of change
It can make a gift to God—dedication of the free will to the doing of God's will
It is characterized by morality and choosingly discriminates between conduct levels
Personality is unique, absolutely unique
Personality responds directly to other-personality presence
It can be added to spirit, illustrating the primacy of the Father
Personality may survive mortal death with identity in the surviving soul
Personality is uniquely conscious of time
L278.d: The paper on personality survival first says that it would be presumptuous to attempt a definition of personality, then calmly recounts fourteen things known about it. It begins with origin: personality is bestowed by the Father or by the Conjoint Actor and may be given to any living energy system that includes mind or spirit. Then come its qualities. Personality is not wholly bound by antecedent causation and is relatively creative; though devoid of identity itself, it unifies identity; it is changeless in the presence of change. Morality, uniqueness, direct response to other personalities, and a unique consciousness of time also characterize it. The eighth item, that personality can make a gift to God, stands at the heart of the list. And personality may survive mortal death with identity in the surviving soul.

L279.t: Three Cosmic Planes on Which Personality Performs
rows: Position status
Functions equally efficiently in the local universe, superuniverse, and central universe
Meaning status
Performs on the levels of the finite, the absonite, and even impinging upon the absolute
Value status
Experientially realized in the progressive realms of the material, the morontial, and the spiritual
L279.d: Personality is bestowed by the Universal Father upon his creatures as a potentially eternal endowment, a divine gift designed to function on many levels and in successive universe situations, from the lowly finite to the highest absonite. It therefore performs on three cosmic planes. Position status is the axis of space: personality functions equally well in the local universe, the superuniverse, and the central universe. Meaning status is the axis of reality levels, reaching through the finite and the absonite to the edge of the absolute. Value status is the axis of experience, realized in the material, morontial, and spiritual realms. The list shows that personality is not bound to any one world but is a continuous reality spanning the whole ascent, which is the very ground of personality survival.

rows: Length
Direction and nature of progression—movement through space and according to time—evolution
Vertical depth
Organismal drives and attitudes, levels of self-realization, reaction to environment
Breadth
The domain of co-ordination, association, and selfhood organization
L280.d: Personality has a perfected range of cosmic dimensional performance, and the dimensions of finite personality are three. The revelator borrows the dimensions of space to describe them. Length represents the direction and nature of progression, movement through space and according to time, which is evolution. Vertical depth embraces organismal drives and attitudes, the levels of self-realization, and reaction to environment. Breadth embraces co-ordination, association, and selfhood organization. The passage goes on to say that length denotes meaning, depth signifies value, and breadth embraces insight, and that the personality of Urantia mortals has a potential of seven dimensions: three finite, three absonite, and one absolute. Much confusion in the study of personality is avoided by remembering that dimensional and spiritual levels are not co-ordinate.

L281.t: Four Things to Remember in the Study of Selfhood
rows: Physical systems
Subordinate
Intellectual systems
Co-ordinate
Personality
Superordinate
The indwelling spiritual force
Potentially directive
L281.d: What should be remembered in the study of selfhood? The revelator sets out in four phrases the order among the elements that make up a human being. Physical systems are subordinate, intellectual systems are co-ordinate, personality is superordinate, and the indwelling spiritual force is potentially directive. The body stands in a serving position, the mind in a co-operating one, personality in a unifying one, while the Adjuster can direct, but only potentially, that is, through human choice. The passage adds that the fact of life comes first and its evaluation or interpretation later: the human child first lives and subsequently thinks about his living. This brief list shows at a glance the order underlying the view of human nature in the Urantia Book.

L282.t: Two Great Phases of Increasing Volitional Dominance
rows: The prefinaliter or God-seeking experience
Augmenting self-realization through identity expansion and cosmic problem solving
The postfinaliter or God-revealing experience
Expanding self-realization by revealing the Supreme Being to God-seeking intelligences
L282.d: The purpose of cosmic evolution is to achieve unity of personality through increasing spirit dominance, through volitional response to the leading of the Thought Adjuster. The revelator divides the path by which an ascending onetime human personality extends volitional dominance over the self and in the universe into two great phases. The first is the prefinaliter or God-seeking experience, augmenting self-realization through identity expansion, cosmic problem solving, and consequent universe mastery. The second is the postfinaliter or God-revealing experience, the creative expansion of self-realization by revealing the Supreme Being of experience to God-seeking intelligences who have not yet attained divine levels of Godlikeness. There is beauty in the pattern: the seeker finally becomes the revealer. Descending personalities attain analogous experiences through their own universe adventures.

L283.t: Three Kinds of Death Concerning Personality Survival
rows: Spiritual (soul) death
Man has finally rejected survival; the Adjuster is released, and the mortal is already dead
Intellectual (mind) death
The essential mind circuits of human will-action have been destroyed
Physical (body and mind) death
The mind ceases to function as an intelligent mechanism; the Adjuster proceeds to Divinington
L283.d: Urantians generally recognize only one kind of death, the physical cessation of life energies, but Paper 112 distinguishes three kinds with regard to personality survival. The measure is not the body but the departure of the indwelling Adjuster. One who has finally rejected survival is already dead from the cosmic standpoint, even while his body lives; and the destruction of the essential mind circuits of will-action is likewise counted as death. Yet a person who loses those circuits may still survive as a soul, according to the prior choosing of the human will. The list shows that true human life is measured not by the pulse of the flesh but by the God-seeking decisions of the will and the soul that holds them.

L284.t: Seven Temporary Assignments of the Adjuster of a Sleeping Survivor
rows: Be mustered into the ranks of vanished Monitors for undisclosed service
Be assigned for a period to the observation of the Paradise regime
Be enrolled in one of the many training schools of Divinington
Be stationed as a student observer on one of the other six sacred spheres
Be assigned to the messenger service of the Personalized Adjusters
Become an associate instructor in the Divinington schools for Monitors of the virgin group
Select a group of possible worlds on which to serve if the human partner rejected survival
L284.d: When a mortal dies, the Adjuster goes to Divinington. If the human ascends in his own individual right on the third period, the Adjuster soon prepares to receive him on the mansion world; but if he belongs to a group to be repersonalized at the end of a dispensation, the waiting is long. This list gives the seven temporary assignments the Adjuster may choose during that interval. Observation and study, messenger service, and even the instruction of other Monitors fill the time, so that the Adjuster keeps serving and growing while it waits. The last item, preparing for the possibility that the human partner has rejected survival, quietly reminds the reader that survival remains a matter of human choice to the end.

L285.t: Three Elements in the Reassembly of a Onetime Material Personality
rows: The fabrication of a suitable form
A morontia energy pattern in which the new survivor can contact nonspiritual reality
The return of the Adjuster
The eternal custodian of your ascending identity returns to the waiting morontia creature
The bestowal of the morontia entity
The seraphic custodian bestows the slumbering immortal soul upon the morontia mind-body form
L285.d: The Urantia Book calls the awakening of a sleeping survivor on the mansion worlds repersonalization. It takes place in the resurrection halls of the morontia receiving planets, in the life-assembly chambers, and requires three elements to come together. First a suitable morontia form is fabricated; then the Adjuster, the eternal custodian of the ascending identity, returns; finally the seraphic custodian bestows the slumbering immortal soul upon that awaiting form. When form, Adjuster, and soul are united, memory, insight, and consciousness, that is, identity, are reassembled. The list carries a quiet assurance: because the Adjuster is present, the one who awakens will be you yourself and not another.

L286.t: Three Intellectual Classes of Mankind in Seraphic Assignment
rows: The subnormal minded
Do not exercise normal will power; cannot comprehend God
The average, normal type of human mind
Grouped in seven classes according to the circles of human progress
The supernormal minded
Those of great decision and undoubted potential of spiritual achievement
L286.d: Originally the seraphim were assigned to the separate Urantia races, but since the bestowal of Michael they are assigned in accordance with human intelligence, spirituality, and destiny. This list gives the three classes behind that arrangement. The subnormal minded have a company of seraphim with a battalion of cherubim to witness that justice and mercy are extended to them. Most men and women, the average and normal, receive ministry according to their progress from the seventh circle toward the first. The supernormal minded, those enrolled in a reserve corps of destiny or who have made the supreme decision, are at once assigned personal seraphim. Notice how angelic care becomes increasingly personal as human decision and growth advance.

L287.t: Seven Unusual Circumstances Behind the Uniqueness of Urantia's Supervision
rows: The life modification status of Urantia
The exigencies of the Lucifer rebellion
The disruptions of the Adamic default
The irregularities growing out of Urantia's being a bestowal world of the Universe Sovereign
The special function of the twenty-four planetary directors
The location on the planet of an archangels' circuit
The more recent designation of Machiventa Melchizedek as vicegerent Planetary Prince
L287.d: Urantia receives proper and effective supervision from the system, constellation, and universe rulers, yet its planetary government is unlike that of any other world in Satania or even in all Nebadon. This list names seven reasons for that uniqueness. The life modification status of the planet, the two failures of the Lucifer rebellion and the Adamic default, and the honor of having been a bestowal world of the Universe Sovereign are woven together. To these are added the special function of the twenty-four planetary directors, the archangels' circuit located on the planet, and the designation of Machiventa Melchizedek as vicegerent Planetary Prince. The paradox of the list is that a world wounded by rebellion has become a place of special universe concern.

L288.t: Twelve Corps of the Master Seraphim of Planetary Supervision
rows: The epochal angels
Oversight of each generation to fit into the mosaic of the age
The progress angels
Initiating the evolutionary progress of the successive social ages
The religious guardians
The "⟦Q 114:6.7⟧angels of the churches⟦/Q⟧"; safe transit of moral values between epochs
The angels of nation life
The "⟦Q 114:6.8⟧angels of the trumpets⟦/Q⟧"; directors of political performances
The angels of the races
The conservation of the evolutionary races of time
The angels of the future
The projection angels, architects of the successive eras
The angels of enlightenment
The fostering of planetary education; mental and moral training
The angels of health
Assistance of mortal agencies for health and the prevention of disease
The home seraphim
Preservation and advancement of the home, the basic institution of civilization
The angels of industry
Fostering industrial development and improving economic conditions
The angels of diversion
Fostering the values of play, humor, and rest
The angels of superhuman ministry
The angels of the angels, ministering to all other superhuman life
L288.d: Introduced by the planetary chief of seraphim himself, these are the twelve angelic corps at work in the superhuman government of Urantia. Beginning with the age, progress, religion, nation, race, and the future, and reaching to education, health, the home, industry, and diversion, nearly every area of human life lies under angelic ministry. Especially interesting is the account of the progress angels and the religious guardians acting as checkmates to each other, balancing the new against the values of the old. The record that many corps have been changed several times shows that angelic service moves with the needs of the age. That there are angels who foster play, humor, and rest is evidence that celestial watchcare reaches into every corner of life.

L289.t: Three Phases of the Absolute Level: The Original, the Actual, the Potential
rows: The Original
The unqualified concept of the First Source and Center, from which all reality takes origin
The Actual
The union of the three Absolutes of actuality: the Second, Third, and Paradise Sources
The Potential
The union of the three Absolutes of potentiality: Deity, Unqualified, and Universal
L289.d: Before explaining the Supreme Being, Paper 115 offers a basic framework for grasping the absolute level. The Original is the source manifestation of the I AM from which all reality takes origin; the Actual and the Potential, each a union of three Absolutes, constitute the actual and the potential revelation of that originality. Their interassociation yields the tensions within infinity that make all universe growth possible. From the time viewpoint, the Actual is that which was and is, the Potential is that which is becoming, and the Original is that which is. Because both are encircuited in the Original, there can be no end to progression. Hence the insight that every human decision actualizes a new reality and opens a new capacity for growth.

L290.t: The Successive Levels of God the Sevenfold
rows: The Creator Sons (and Creative Spirits)
The Ancients of Days
The Seven Master Spirits
The Supreme Being
The Conjoint Actor
The Eternal Son
The Universal Father
L290.d: Unqualified Paradise Deity is incomprehensible to the creatures of time and space, so Paradise Deity attenuates and qualifies the extra-Paradise personalizations of divinity, bringing the Supreme Creators into existence. This is the origin of God the Sevenfold. The list is written in the order in which mortal man encounters its levels, from below upward. The first three, the Creator Sons, the Ancients of Days, and the Seven Master Spirits, are the Supreme Creators; the last three are the Paradise Deities; and the Supreme Being stands between them as the maximum revelation of Deity to the seven superuniverses. The list shows that God does not remain only a distant Infinite but draws near at every step, like a ladder up which man may climb.

L291.t: Three Agencies Through Which the Paradise Deities Function
rows: The mind focalizations of the Third Source and Center
The mind presences of the Conjoint Actor holding energy and spirit together
The personality revelations of the Second Source and Center
Bestowal incarnations fusing the divine nature of a Creator with creature nature
The indwelling presences of the First Source and Center
Fragments of the Father unifying the evolving creatures with God on Paradise
L291.d: The Paradise Deities not only act directly in their gravity circuits throughout the grand universe but also participate in the evolutions of time through various agencies and manifestations. This list names three of them, in the order of the Third, Second, and First Sources and Centers. The mind of the Conjoint Actor is the vital link connecting matter and spirit; the bestowals of the Sons unify divinity descensions with creature ascensions; and the indwelling fragments of the Father actually unify mortal man with God on Paradise. The heart of the list is the statement that when divinity becomes like humanity, there is the possibility that humanity can become divine. Notice also that all three ways converge in the emergence of the Supreme Being.

L292.t: The Sevenfold Controllers of the Grand Universe
rows: The Master Physical Controllers
The Supreme Power Centers
The Supreme Power Directors
The Almighty Supreme
The God of Action, the Infinite Spirit
The Isle of Paradise
The Source of Paradise, the Universal Father
L292.d: God the Sevenfold encompasses the controllers as well as the creators of the grand universe. This list gives the seven groups that form its physical-control level, beginning with the Master Physical Controllers and rising through the power centers and power directors to the Almighty Supreme, the Infinite Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, and the Universal Father, the Source of Paradise. Set beside the levels of the Sevenfold, it shows that the physical order, as well as the spiritual, is unified in Deity. The Almighty Supreme is now evolving as the overcontroller of the physical power of the grand universe, and the final attainment of material equilibrium is conjectured to signify the completion of that evolution. The struggle for perfection pertains to energy and mass as well as to mind and spirit.

L293.t: Three Avenues of Creature Approach to Supremacy
rows: The Paradise Citizens
Descend through Havona, discovering the activities of the Supreme Creator Personalities
The time-space ascenders
Come up from the evolutionary universes and approach the Supreme in traversing Havona
The Havona natives
Comprehend the Supreme through contacts with descending and ascending pilgrims
L293.d: There is no approach to the Supreme except through experience. This list gives the three avenues by which creatures approach Supremacy in the current epochs, and all three pass through Havona. The Paradise Citizens descend from above, the time-space ascenders come up from below, and the Havona natives, standing in the middle, meet pilgrims from both directions and harmonize their differing viewpoints. The Urantia Book teaches that God the Father can be found by any individual, but that God the Supreme will be found by all creatures simultaneously in the far-distant time of universal perfection. Until then, the fruits of the spirit are the substance of the Supreme as he is realizable in human experience. The deeper meaning of the list is that finding the Supreme is a shared journey, not a solitary one.

L294.t: Three Problems Inherent in the Concept of the Future of the Supreme
rows: The Unqualified Supervisors could hardly be deitized before his completed evolution
Even now they qualifiedly exercise the sovereignty of supremacy in settled universes
The Supreme could hardly function in the Trinity Ultimate before complete actuality
The Trinity Ultimate is even now a qualified reality, with Qualified Vicegerents
The Supreme is not completely real to universe creatures
He is quite real to the Sevenfold Deity
L294.d: Paper 117 presents a concept of the future in which the Supreme, his evolution completed, becomes a member of the Ultimate Trinity. While calling it an entirely proper concept, the revelators frankly point out three problems inherent in it. All three share one form: something that should not yet be complete is already functioning in some measure. The authors suggest that on the upper limits of the finite, where time conjoins transcended time, there may be a blurring and blending of sequence, so that the Supreme can reflect his future back to the created levels as the Immanence of the Projected Incomplete. Striking is the comparison with the Thought Adjusters, which are veritable predictions of man's future universe attainments throughout all eternity.

L295.t: Three Superfinite Possibilities for Universe Manifestation of the Supreme
rows: Absonite collaboration in the first experiential Trinity
Coabsolute relationship in the second experiential Trinity
Coinfinite participation in the Trinity of Trinities
L295.d: The Supreme Being is the God of the finite, yet his destiny does not end in the finite. This list gives three possibilities for his universe manifestation beyond the finite, in the order of absonite, coabsolute, and coinfinite. He collaborates on the absonite level in the first experiential Trinity, enters a coabsolute relationship in the second experiential Trinity, and finally participates in the Trinity of Trinities. The revelators candidly confess that they have no satisfactory concept as to what this last item really means. The following text says that when the grand universe is settled in light and life, the thrilling adventures of evolution will seem to end, but the enigma of God the Ultimate will soon issue a new challenge. The direction of the list is that growth has no end.

L296.t: Seven Statements Concerning the Several Natures of Deity
rows: The Father
Self-existent self
The Son
Coexistent self
The Spirit
Conjoint-existent self
The Supreme
Evolutionary-experiential self
The Sevenfold
Self-distributive divinity
The Ultimate
Transcendental-experiential self
The Absolute
Existential-experiential self
L296.d: Paper 118 opens by defining the several natures of Deity in seven brief statements. The first three, Father, Son, and Spirit, are existential Deity, respectively self-existent, coexistent, and conjoint-existent self. The remaining four concern experience: the Supreme is evolutionary-experiential self, the Sevenfold is self-distributive divinity, the Ultimate is transcendental-experiential self, and the Absolute is existential-experiential self. It is noteworthy that the Sevenfold alone is called not a self but a divinity that distributes itself. Paired with the seven meanings of the word God in the Foreword, this list compresses the framework of the Urantia Book's teaching about Deity, which moves from the existential to the experiential.

L297.t: The Threefold Basic Constitution of Causation
rows: Activation of static potentials
The establishment of destiny in the Universal Absolute by the actions of the Deity Absolute
Eventuation of universe capacities
The transformation of undifferentiated potentials into segregated and defined plans
Creation and evolution of universe actuals
The Supreme Creators effect time transmutations of matured potentials into experiential actuals
L297.d: Disregarding existentials, causation as it operates on the finite level in this universe age has three stages. First, in consequence of the volitional mandates of the Paradise Trinity, the Deity Absolute activates static potentials and establishes destiny. Next, the Ultimacy of Deity and the agencies of the transcendental level, such as the Architects of the Master Universe, segregate those potentials into defined plans. Finally, the Supreme Creators, such as the Creator Sons, transmute matured potentials into experiential actuals in time. Hence the Creator Sons are, in the cosmic sense, transformative creators, though from the finite viewpoint they certainly can and do create. The list shows that creation is not a single moment but a process descending through absolute, transcendental, and finite levels.

L298.t: Three Factors That Modify Man's Viewpoint of the Natural Order
rows: Man's augmenting vision
Enlarging comprehension of material facts, meaningful ideas, and valuable ideals
Man's increasing control
The gradual accumulation of knowledge of material laws and spiritual purposes
Man's universe integration
Increased insight and achievement bring closer harmony with the presences of Supremacy
L298.d: In the beginnings of an evolutionary world, natural law often appears cruel, heartless, and indifferent to all that is true, beautiful, and good. This passage on providence says that as humanity progresses in planetary development, that viewpoint is modified by three factors. Man's vision enlarges, his control grows through knowledge of matter and spirit, and at last he comes into harmony with the unifying presences of Supremacy. Savage man was helpless before natural forces; semicivilized man is destroying superstition by science; civilized man will someday achieve relative mastery of the physical forces of his planet. On worlds settled in light and life, providence has become an actuality. Providence is not a miracle dropped from heaven but the order revealed when man begins to live according to the trend of the universes.

L299.t: Two Things Providence Must Ever Be
rows: Partial
Due to the incompleteness of the actualization of the Supreme Being
Unpredictable
Due to the fluctuations in creature attitude, causing variable reciprocal response in the Supreme
L299.d: Providence is in part the overcontrol of the incomplete Supreme manifested in the incomplete universes. It must therefore ever be partial and unpredictable: the Supreme Being himself is still being actualized, and creature attitudes vary from level to level, causing apparently variable reciprocal response in the Supreme. The text goes on to say that when men pray for providential intervention, many times the answer to their prayer is their own changed attitudes toward life. Providence is not whimsical, fantastic, or magical. It is the slow and sure emergence of the mighty sovereign of the finite universes, the sure and certain march of the galaxies of space and the personalities of time toward the goals of eternity.

L300.t: The Seven Bestowals of Christ Michael
rows: Melchizedek bestowal
The united will of the Father, Son, and Spirit
Lanonandek bestowal
The will of the Father and the Son
Adamic bestowal
The will of the Father and the Spirit
Seraphic bestowal
The will of the Son and the Spirit
Uversa mortal bestowal
The will of the Conjoint Actor
Morontia mortal bestowal
The will of the Eternal Son
Urantia material bestowal
The will of the Universal Father, as a mortal of flesh and blood
L300.d: Gavalia, chief of the Evening Stars of Nebadon, narrates the seven bestowals of Michael, which descended from the highest Melchizedek order down to the mortals of flesh and blood. A Creator Son does not assume full sovereignty of his new creation until his seven creature bestowals have been completed and certified by the Ancients of Days. Their purpose is that the Creator acquire the viewpoint of his own creatures by actual experience, becoming a wise, sympathetic, just, and understanding sovereign. Each bestowal also revealed one of the will aspects of Deity personalized in the Seven Master Spirits, and on Urantia he lived the will of the Universal Father as a mortal. The life of Jesus was the climax of this long journey.

L301.t: The Bestowal Limitations: Immanuel's Nine Counsels to Michael
rows: Grow up on Urantia as a child of the realm, subject to the will of your Paradise Father
As the Son of Man, technically terminate the Lucifer rebellion in Satania
Accept the title 'Planetary Prince of Urantia'; atone for the Caligastia betrayal and Adamic default
End the bestowal with a dispensational judgment and the resurrection of the sleeping survivors
Function largely as a teacher, first liberating and inspiring man's spiritual nature
Set rebellion-segregated man spiritually free; pour out the Spirit of Truth
Live a life for the instruction and edification of all your universe
Reveal God in the flesh, and make a new revelation of man to God
Remaining potentially a Creator Son, refrain from any superhuman will-to-attainment
L301.d: Just before Michael began his seventh bestowal on Urantia, his elder brother Immanuel delivered these instructions in accordance with the usages of Sonarington. The nine items narrow from the large to the particular. They first address the course of the whole bestowal, the termination of the Lucifer rebellion, the title of Planetary Prince, and the dispensational judgment; then they counsel the role of teacher, the outpouring of the Spirit of Truth, and a life lived for the whole universe. The eighth item sums up the mission: to reveal God to man and man to God by a life devoted to the Father's will. The last is a caution to refrain from any superhuman will-to-power, since the creator prerogatives remained with him. Here lies the reason Jesus withheld miracles and walked the path of an ordinary man.

L302.t: Eight Advices Concerning Minor Phases of the Mortal Life
rows: Give attention to things practical and immediately helpful to your fellow men
Give precedence to the accepted customs of family life of your day
Confine efforts to spiritual regeneration and intellectual emancipation; avoid political entanglements
Never interfere with the normal and orderly progressive evolution of the Urantia races
Avoid an organized cult or crystallized religion; your teachings are the common heritage
Leave no writings behind you; enjoin your associates to make no images of yourself
You will probably not enter the marriage relation; leave no human offspring
All other details are committed to the Adjuster, the divine spirit, and human reason-judgment
L302.d: After his nine counsels on the bestowal as a whole, Immanuel added eight further advices arrived at in consultation with Gabriel. These concern minor phases of the mortal life: family, social order, politics, religious organization, writings and images, and marriage. The common principle is not to interfere with the normal evolution of the races and to leave behind nothing that might become a stereotyped system of belief or an occasion for idolatry. The list explains why Jesus wrote nothing, left no likeness, did not marry, and avoided political entanglements. The last item commits all other details to the leading of the Adjuster and the judgment of his human mind. The aim was that his life and teachings become the common heritage of all religions and all peoples.

L303.t: The Threefold Influence That Unified European Civilization
rows: The Roman political and social systems
The Grecian language and culture, and philosophy to a certain extent
The rapidly spreading influence of Jewish religious and moral teachings
L303.d: Nothing like the civilization of the times of Jesus has been seen in the Occident before or since. European civilization was unified and co-ordinated under the threefold influence of Roman political and social systems, Grecian language and culture, and Jewish religious and moral teachings. The entire Mediterranean world was a unified empire; good roads interconnected the major centers, the seas were cleared of pirates, and a great era of trade and travel was advancing. Rome supplied roads and order, Greece a common language and thought, and Judaism the one God and a sturdy morality. The list shows that the time of Michael's bestowal was a moment when the gospel could spread most rapidly, though beneath the superficial prosperity most inhabitants languished in poverty.

L304.t: Five Well-Defined Strata of Mediterranean Society
rows: The aristocracy
The upper classes with money and official power, the privileged and ruling groups
The business groups
Merchant princes, bankers, traders, and international merchants
The small middle class
Small but influential; the moral backbone of the early Christian church
The free proletariat
Proud of their freedom but forced to compete with slave labor
The slaves
Half the population; many superior individuals quickly made their way up
L304.d: Although the social and economic condition of the Roman state was not of the highest order, its widespread domestic peace and prosperity was propitious for Michael's bestowal. In the first century after Christ, Mediterranean society consisted of five well-defined strata, from the aristocracy down to the slaves. Notably, the small but influential middle class provided the moral backbone of the early Christian church, while the church itself was largely composed of the lower classes and slaves. Half the population were slaves, yet superior slaves could save their wages, purchase their freedom, and rise to high positions. The people were generally not class conscious and did not regard these distinctions as unjust. Christianity therefore spread not as an economic movement of the depressed classes but as a spiritual one.

L305.t: Four Schools of Philosophy That Dominated the Gentile World
rows: The Epicurean
Dedicated to the pursuit of happiness; combated ignorant superstition
The Stoic
A controlling Reason-Fate; a sublime morality, but never a religion
The Cynic
Remnants of Melchizedek's teachings; "⟦Q 121:4.4⟧man could save himself if he would⟦/Q⟧"
The Skeptic
Knowledge fallacious, conviction impossible; a purely negative attitude
L305.d: The gentile world of Jesus' day was dominated by four great philosophies, all more or less derived from the earlier Platonism of the Greeks. The Epicureans pursued happiness and combated superstition; the Stoics ascended to a sublime morality never since transcended by any purely human system of philosophy. Yet while the Stoics professed to be the offspring of God, they failed to envisage themselves as the children of a loving Father. The Cynics, heirs of remnants of Machiventa Melchizedek's teachings, preached in fields and market places and prepared the way for the later Christian missionaries. The Skeptics remained in a purely negative attitude. These were philosophies for the strong and the wise, not religions of salvation for the poor and the weak, and in this they stand in contrast to the gospel of Jesus.

L306.t: Four Common Characteristics of the Mystery Religions
rows: Some mythical legend, a mystery, usually of some god's life, death, and return to life
Nonnational and interracial; personal and fraternal, giving rise to religious brotherhoods
Elaborate ceremonies of initiation and impressive sacraments of worship
Invariably promised salvation: deliverance from evil and survival after death
L306.d: Among the religions of the Occident in Jesus' day, the mystery cults that flooded in from the Levant enamored the spiritually hungry common people and became the accepted belief of the lower classes of the Greco-Roman world. They spelled the end of national beliefs and gave birth to numerous personal cults. This list names their four common characteristics: a mythical legend of some god's death and return to life, a fraternal bond transcending nation and race, elaborate initiations and sacraments, and the promise of individual salvation. The text warns against confusing the teachings of Jesus with the mysteries. Yet their popularity revealed a real hunger for personal religion and individual righteousness, and so prepared the way for Jesus, who truly brought the bread of life.

L307.t: Three Ways Paul's Christianity Was Superior to the Mysteries
rows: Paul taught a moral redemption, an ethical salvation, and forsook magic rites
It offered salvation from sorrow and death, and deliverance from sin with a righteous character
It was founded not upon myths but upon a historic fact: the bestowal of Michael
L307.d: Seeking to utilize the widespread adherence to the mystery religions, Paul made certain adaptations of the teachings of Jesus. The resulting Christianity was a compromise of Jesus' teachings, yet even that compromise was superior to the best in the mysteries in three ways. It taught a moral redemption and ethical salvation in place of magic rites; it promised not only salvation from death but deliverance from sin and the endowment of a righteous character; and it was founded not upon myths but upon the historic fact that the Son of God had actually been bestowed upon mankind. The text adds that Judaism, the teachings of Jesus, and Paul's Christianity were the first European religions to insist upon both morals and ethics. The list shows how great the power of the gospel remained even in compromised form.

L308.t: Three Teachings Blended with the Gospel in Antioch Christianity
rows: The philosophic reasoning of the Greek proselytes to Judaism, including concepts of the eternal life
The mystery cults, especially the Mithraic doctrines of redemption, atonement, and salvation by sacrifice
The sturdy morality of the established Jewish religion
L308.d: As it was embodied in Paul's cult of Antioch Christianity, the gospel of Jesus did not travel in its pure form. This list names the three teachings that became blended with it: the philosophic reasoning of Greek proselytes, the mystery cults' doctrines of sacrifice and redemption, and the sturdy morality of Judaism. In particular, the Mithraic doctrine of salvation by the sacrifice made by some god became a foundation of later Christian atonement theology. This blending made Christianity acceptable to Greeks, Jews, and devotees of the mysteries alike, and it spread rapidly. But the price was that Jesus' simple gospel of the fatherhood of God and the brotherhood of man was overshadowed by a religion about Jesus. The list is a key for distinguishing Christianity from the religion of Jesus.

L309.t: The Origin of the Four Gospels
rows: The Gospel by Mark
John Mark wrote from his and Peter's memory for the church at Rome, A.D. 68
The Gospel of Matthew
Written by Isador, Matthew's disciple, at Pella for Jewish Christians, A.D. 71
The Gospel by Luke
Luke, the physician and gentile convert of Paul, wrote in Achaia in 82
The Gospel of John
Inspired by John; written by his associate Nathan, begun A.D. 101
L309.d: The Urantia Book states concretely the circumstances in which the four New Testament Gospels originated. Mark's record is in reality the Gospel according to Simon Peter and became the written basis of all subsequent Gospel narratives. Matthew's Gospel was written not by the apostle but by his disciple Isador; crediting it to Matthew was no deception but the custom by which pupils honored their teachers. Luke's Gospel is in some ways the Gospel according to Paul and presents the Master as the friend of publicans and sinners. John did not write the Gospel bearing his name, but he inspired it, and it records much of Jesus' work in Judea and around Jerusalem not contained in the other records. Knowing each Gospel's readers and viewpoint helps one understand their differences more deeply.

L310.t: Seven Stages of a Child's Life Among the Galilean Jews
rows: The newborn child, the first to the eighth day
The suckling child
The weaned child
The period of dependence on the mother, up to the end of the fifth year
The beginning independence of the child; with sons, the father assuming responsibility for education
The adolescent youths and maidens
The young men and the young women
L310.d: There were few homes in the gentile world of that day that could give a child a better intellectual, moral, and religious training than the Jewish homes of Galilee. These Jews had a systematic program for rearing and educating their children, and these seven stages were its framework. Until the fifth birthday the mother bore the responsibility for a child's training; thereafter, if the child were a boy, the father took charge of his education. In the year he turned five, Jesus entered upon this fifth stage, and Mary formally turned him over to Joseph for further instruction. That Jesus grew up within such devout and orderly home education shows that his human development was built on the wisdom of an ordinary Jewish family.

L311.t: Five Questions the Boy Jesus Asked in the Temple
rows: What really exists in the holy of holies, behind the veil?
Why should mothers in Israel be segregated from the male temple worshipers?
If God is a father who loves his children, why all this slaughter of animals?
Is it consistent to permit secular barter and trade in the temple?
Is the Messiah to be a temporal prince, or the light of life in a spiritual kingdom?
L311.d: Having gone up to Jerusalem for the Passover, the boy Jesus spent days in the temple with the scribes and teachers. On the third day many spectators gathered, having heard of the youth from Galilee, and the entire attention of the chief discussion group became focused on his questions. This list gives five among his many questions. Asking about the holy of holies, the segregation of mothers, the slaughter of animals, trade in the temple, and the nature of the Messiah, they anticipate themes of his later public ministry. He made few comments on the remarks of his elders, conveying his teaching by the questions he asked, and he never took unfair advantage of an opponent. Already as a youth he sought not to win arguments but to proclaim everlasting truth.

L312.t: The Twofold Purpose of Michael's Bestowal on Urantia
rows: The mastering of the experience of living the full life of a human creature in mortal flesh
The revelation of the Universal Father to mortals and their more effective leading to him
L312.d: At the outset of the paper on Jesus' early manhood, the reader is asked always to be mindful of the twofold purpose of Michael's bestowal on Urantia. The first concerns Michael himself: mastering the experience of living the full life of a human creature in mortal flesh, and thus completing his sovereignty in Nebadon. The second concerns mankind: revealing the Universal Father to the mortals of time and space and leading them more effectively to a better understanding of him. All other creature benefits and universe advantages were incidental and secondary to these purposes. It is striking that even the death on the cross does not appear in this list. The Urantia Book asks that Jesus' life be read above all as an event of living and of revelation.

L313.t: Three Foundations for the Rapid Spread of Christianity in Europe
rows: The choosing and holding of Simon Peter as an apostle
The talk in Jerusalem with Stephen, whose death led to the winning of Saul of Tarsus
The preliminary preparation of thirty Romans for the subsequent leadership of the new religion in Rome and throughout the empire
L313.d: During his Mediterranean journey Jesus stayed in Rome and taught thirty-two religious leaders, most often one by one. Thirty of them later became pivotal individuals in establishing Christianity in Rome, and some helped turn the chief Mithraic temple into the city's first Christian church. The revelators recognize just these three factors as setting the stage for the spread of Christianity. Strikingly, neither Stephen nor the thirty ever realized that the man they had once talked with was the one whose name became the subject of their own teaching. Great history was prepared in quiet personal encounters.

L314.t: Ten Different Methods of Amassing Material Wealth
rows: Inherited wealth
Riches derived from parents and other ancestors
Discovered wealth
Riches from the uncultivated resources of mother earth
Trade wealth
A fair profit in the exchange and barter of material goods
Unfair wealth
Riches from the unfair exploitation or enslavement of one's fellows
Interest wealth
Income from the fair and just earning possibilities of invested capital
Genius wealth
Rewards of the creative and inventive endowments of the human mind
Accidental wealth
From the generosity of one's fellows or the circumstances of life
Stolen wealth
Secured by unfairness, dishonesty, theft, or fraud
Trust funds
Wealth lodged in your hands by your fellows for some specific use
Earned wealth
The fair and just reward of your own daily efforts of mind and body
L314.d: In Rome a wealthy Roman asked Jesus whether he should keep his wealth or give it away. Jesus first urged him to regard his wealth as a trust and to analyze honestly whence it came, offering these ten sources. The list mixes legitimate sources such as inheritance, discovery, trade, interest, genius, and labor with illegitimate ones such as exploitation and theft. Jesus counseled him to divide his fortune approximately into these ten grand divisions and to administer each according to the laws of justice, equity, and fairness. He added that when in honest doubt one should let decisions favor those in need and those who suffer undeserved hardships. Jesus repeatedly stressed that this advice was offered only to this man for his personal guidance.

L315.t: Ten Counsels of Jesus to the Rich Man Concerning His Wealth
rows: Inherited wealth
Consider its sources; transmit legitimate wealth honestly to succeeding generations
Wealth of discovery
Provide for sharing discoveries with the largest possible number of fellow men
Trade wealth
Take a fair profit, judged by justice, honesty, and fairness
Wealth of oppression
Restore riches from the sweat of oppressed men to those thus robbed
Interest
First cleanse your capital; never stoop to the practice of usury
Genius wealth
Do not lay claim to an unfair portion of such rewards
Accidental riches
Regard them as a trust for the benefit of one's social or economic group
Wealth from fraud
Make haste to restore all ill-gotten gains to the rightful owners
Trusteeship
A solemn and sacred responsibility; do not hazard such a trust
Earnings of your own efforts
Truly your own, if your work has been done in fairness and equity
L315.d: After having the rich man analyze the ten sources of his wealth, Jesus, at his request, counseled him on the right attitude toward each. The principle is simple: use in equity what was legitimately gained, restore what was unjustly gained, and administer faithfully what has been entrusted. The heir is a trustee representing the past generation; the discoverer and the genius owe something to ancestors, progeny, and race; accidental riches are a trust for one's group. Only the earnings of honest personal labor are truly one's own. Jesus says it will ever be impossible to establish rules applicable equally to all problems of the equitable distribution of wealth. But if one recognizes man as a brother and does by him as he would be done by, the commonplace dictates of justice, honesty, and fairness will show the way.

L316.t: Two Ways Jesus Might Manifest Himself to the World
rows: His own way
The way most pleasant and profitable for the immediate needs of this world
The Father's way
The exemplification of a farseeing ideal of creature life visualized by the Paradise administration
L316.d: During the forty days in the mountain wilderness after his baptism, Jesus arrived, one by one, at the great decisions that would control the remainder of his earth life. Gabriel had reminded him that there were two ways in which he might manifest himself to the world should he tarry on Urantia: his own way and the Father's way. The choice had nothing to do with his universe sovereignty or the termination of the Lucifer rebellion; sovereignty was already settled and only awaited his demand. Yet it was indicated that it would afford his Paradise brother, Immanuel, great satisfaction if he finished his career as nobly begun, always subject to the Father's will. On the third day of his isolation Jesus promised himself always to choose the Father's will, and he kept that resolve to the bitter end.

L317.t: Two Opposing Courses of Conduct in Jesus' Heart
rows: A strong desire to win his people and the whole world to believe in him
To live and work as his Father would approve, revealing the Father's divine character of love
L317.d: In planning the remainder of his earth life during the forty days, Jesus was always torn in his human heart by two opposing courses of conduct. One was a strong desire to win his people and the whole world to believe in him and accept his new spiritual kingdom. He well knew their ideas concerning the coming Messiah, and by meeting those expectations he might easily have won many. The other was to live and work as his Father would approve, to serve other worlds in need, and, in establishing the kingdom, to reveal the Father and show forth his divine character of love. This inner conflict shows how fully human Jesus was. He always chose the second course, and so walked the lonely path of refusing to become the Messiah many expected.

rows: Matthew Levi
The customs collector of Capernaum; selected by Andrew
Thomas Didymus
Fisherman of Tarichea, onetime carpenter and stone mason; selected by Philip
James Alpheus
Fisherman and farmer of Kheresa; selected by James Zebedee
Judas Alpheus
Twin brother of James Alpheus, a fisherman; selected by John Zebedee
Simon Zelotes
High officer of the Zealots, formerly a merchant; selected by Peter
Judas Iscariot
Only son of wealthy Jewish parents in Jericho; invited by Nathaniel
L318.d: The first six apostles, called by Jesus himself, were each to select one new apostle. This list gives the second six chosen in that way: Andrew brought Matthew, Philip brought Thomas, the Zebedee brothers brought the Alpheus twins, Peter brought Simon Zelotes, and Nathaniel invited Judas Iscariot. Their backgrounds are strikingly varied: a customs collector, fishermen, a carpenter, farmers, a Zealot officer, and a young man experienced in finances. The record notes that Judas Iscariot was the only Judean among the twelve apostles. Jesus spent a full day with the six, answering their questions and listening to their reports. A distinctive feature of the list is that the apostolic corps was completed by men calling other men.

L319.t: Three Things the Apostles Were Enjoined Not to Discuss
rows: The work and imprisonment of John the Baptist
The voice at the baptism: "⟦Q 138:8.4⟧Only those who heard the voice may refer to it⟦/Q⟧"
